title: Reservation intake: handshake, throughput SLOs and autoscale guardrails
creator: Ava McKenna
description:
Problem statement:
Teams requesting dedicated capacity today submit a reservation form and wait for manual approvals. There is no standardized ‘handshake’ that codifies throughput guarantees, expected autoscale behaviour, and fleet-level controls. This causes long lead times, inconsistent SLO promises, and operational surprises when traffic spikes or when autoscale thresholds are misconfigured.

Goal:
Design a provisioning workflow and intake handshake that: (1) collects minimal but sufficient signals to size guaranteed throughput, (2) maps those signals to an autoscaling policy template and a fleet control whitelist, and (3) provides an approval matrix and preflight simulation that verifies expected latency and cost under representative workloads. The outcome should reduce lead time, make guarantees predictable, and reduce emergency scaling interventions.

Scope:
- Intake form fields and validation rules (traffic profile, p50/p95 latency targets, burst windows, retention of KV cache, routing region).
- Autoscale policy templates tied to workload classes (steady, spiky, burstable) with clear throttle/fallback rules.
- Throughput guarantee contract wording and metrics (tokens/sec, concurrent requests, allowed tail latency).
- Fleet guardrails: node class constraints, quantization profile allowance, hot-fallback model variants, and rollback triggers.
- Preflight simulation harness (synthetic replay against a sandbox fleet) and required artifacts for sign-off.
- Approval matrix by cost delta, commitment length, and customer tier.
acceptance_criteria: A validated intake form exists in the Console and returns a sizing estimate within 24 hours for >90% of submissions.
Three autoscale policy templates (steady, spiky, burstable) defined in the spec and implemented as reusable config snippets.
Throughput guarantee SLA language drafted and legal-reviewed; mapping from intake signals to SLA parameters automated.
A preflight simulation runs end-to-end in sandbox showing expected p50/p95 token latency and estimated monthly cost; results populate the reservation ticket.
Approval matrix implemented: auto-approve for small deltas (<10% committed capacity) and human review lanes for high-cost or long-commitment requests.
Dashboard surfaced in Console showing reservation status, expected vs observed throughput, and autoscale events post-provisioning.
Rollback/playbook documented for scenario where observed latency >SLO for two consecutive 10-minute windows.
Cross-functional sign-off from Eng (serving/runtime), Reliability, Legal (SLA wording), and Sales/CS for customer impact classification.
updates: 2026-03-10: Created initial ticket after product sync—identified high lead-time as root cause for 3 recent support escalations.
2026-03-11: Kickoff with Serving runtime and Reliability teams. Agreed to prototype two autoscale templates first (steady + spiky). Action: ENG to draft template configs (ENG-1842).
2026-03-12: Draft intake form fields circulated — added explicit 'burst window' and 'sample prompt set' as required inputs. PM requested a lightweight estimator to return initial throughput bands.

2026-03-13: Decided on preflight simulation approach: replay sampled customer traffic against a fenced sandbox fleet using the same quant/ops profiles. Eng will surface synthetic run logs to ticket (ENG-3327).
2026-03-14: Legal began SLA wording review. Early feedback: avoid hard 'unbounded' fallbacks; must include deterministic fallback model variant list and cost delta disclosure.
Blockers: Need a small sandbox fleet with cost tracking enabled for realistic preflight runs. Infra scheduling for sandbox needs prioritization.
risks: Under-estimation of bursty workloads leading to SLA breaches and manual emergency scaling.
Overly conservative sizing that bloats committed cost and increases friction for customers.
Complex approval matrix causing human bottlenecks if automation rules are too narrow.
Inaccurate preflight simulation if sampled workloads are not representative of production prompts.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (pilot): Manual intake with PM-assigned reviewers for 3 strategic customers — validate estimator accuracy.
Phase 1 (automation): Implement auto-sizing API and autoscale template binding; enable auto-approve for low-risk requests.
Phase 2 (scale): Surface in Console for all sales-assisted reservations; add analytics and default retention for preflight traces.
Phase 3 (opt): Add machine-learned sizing suggestions using historical request patterns and model execution profiles.
test_plan: Unit tests for intake validation rules (missing burst window, invalid latency target).
Integration test: run preflight replay in sandbox; assert p95 latency within 20% of estimate for 90% of runs.
Chaos test: simulate a sudden 3x traffic spike during preflight and validate fallback model variant triggers.
Cost verification: compare simulated monthly cost estimate against billed sandbox cost within 15%.
Post-provision smoke: verify autoscale events trigger and KV cache warm-up completes within expected window.
decision_log: 2026-03-11: Chose three canonical workload classes rather than dozens of bespoke templates to keep approval surface small.
2026-03-12: Required 'sample prompt set' as part of intake to improve preflight representativeness.
2026-03-13: Preflight will run against a fenced sandbox fleet with identical kernel/quantization settings to the requested profile.
2026-03-14: SLA wording must include an explicit fallback behaviour and cost disclosure — Legal flagged this as non-negotiable.
next_steps: ENG: Deliver initial autoscale template PR and a lightweight sizing estimator endpoint (owner: @samir). Target: 2026-03-21 (ENG-1842).
Infra: Provision a 24/7 sandbox fleet with cost tracking enabled and attach to sandbox dashboard. Target: 2026-03-20 (ENG-3327).
PM: Finalize intake form fields and build Console prototype for pilot customers. Target: 2026-03-18.
Legal: Complete SLA language review and produce a short 'customer-friendly' contract snippet for sales. Target: 2026-03-22.
Design: Mock minimal Console flow for reservation creation + preflight results summary. Target: 2026-03-17.
